title: The math of the housing gap

captions.instagram:
Per JemRock research, the world needs 96,000 new homes a day. That's about 4,000 an hour, 67 a minute, more than one every second.

Behind that math are people. It's why our mission at JemRock is to change how the world produces housing. UN-Habitat counts 2.8 billion people without adequate housing.

Swipe for the full breakdown, and save the 4 questions to ask any housing number.

captions.linkedin:
Before you react to a housing number, ask who reported it and what it counts.

Per JemRock research, the global housing deficit is 155 million units, projected to reach 240 million by 2030. Keeping up means about 96,000 homes a day: more than one every second.

UN-Habitat counts 2.8 billion people without adequate housing, 1.1 billion in slums or informal settlements, and more than 300 million who are homeless.

Speed is part of the answer. McKinsey (2019) found modular construction can be 20-50% faster. Our design target for BUILT® is more than 50% faster timelines. That is a target, not a result yet.

Four questions for any housing number: Who reported it? What does it count? What year is it for? Is it a result or a target?
